clue.text: Probing viral disease, doctor with a carrier

indicators.note: probing means poking into something, so the doctor and the a go inside the disease

parts.note: a bug is an informal word for a virus or infection
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor carrying something while investigating an outbreak of a viral illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Probing' signals the container; 'carrier' sounds medical, as in a disease carrier, but here it is a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumbag is a small pouch worn on a belt round the waist, used for carrying things.

clue.text: Custom from America, say, taken up

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: A tradition imported from the United States and adopted here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established practice or habit, a synonym of custom.

clue.text: Swear sheep is dancing with lamb

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so sheep and lamb are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A farmyard scene of a sheep frolicking alongside a lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges SHEEP and LAMB together.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaspheme is to use profane language about sacred things, a kind of swearing.

clue.text: Coarse Yankee supporting Republican in win

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so this letter comes last
in places the Republican inside the word for win

parts.note: to gain is to win or obtain
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American backing a Republican to victory, described as crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts Y below GRAIN in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Grainy texture is rough and granular, so it describes something coarse.

clue.text: Work with a venture that's most shady

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a quest is an expedition or venture

explanation.surface: Describing a business deal as the dodgiest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means not letting light through, so the most opaque thing is the most shady or dark.

clue.text: Personification of London banker?

parts.note: a banker in crosswords can be a river, something with banks; the river through London personified as an elderly man

explanation.surface: Someone who embodies the City's financiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' points to finance, but here it is a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames flowing through London is traditionally personified as an old bearded man figure.

clue.text: Bitterness from a baseless misdemeanour over New Year

indicators.note: baseless means losing the bottom, and in a down clue the final letter is the base

parts.note: a misdemeanour is a minor crime
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
NY is a standard abbreviation for New Year

explanation.surface: Resentment caused by a petty offence committed just before New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baseless' drops the last letter of CRIME, leaving CRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is harsh or bitter feeling and speech, a direct synonym.

clue.text: University with refurbished bar north of city

indicators.note: refurbished means done up anew, so the letters of bar are rearranged

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A university with a renovated pub, situated north of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refurbished' turns BAR into RBA; 'north of city' looks like a location, but only 'north' gives N and 'of city' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban is the adjective meaning relating to a town or metropolis.

clue.text: Reserve opinion for matter

parts.note: a sub is a substitute or reserve player
a stance is a position or opinion

explanation.surface: Holding back one's view on a particular issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Substance means physical material, which is what matter is.

clue.text: Beast Adam learns about

indicators.note: about can mean around in a jumbled way, so Adam learns is rearranged

explanation.surface: A biblical picture of Adam getting to know an animal in Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ADAM LEARNS.
explanation.definitionFit: A salamander is an amphibian, so it is a creature or animal.

clue.text: Graduate close to pet project

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
by means near or close to

explanation.surface: A graduate living near a favoured scheme of theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's baby is informally their pet project, a scheme they nurture personally.

clue.text: Asian animal's sweep blocking comeback of viper

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, so one word sits inside the other
comeback of means coming back, read backwards

parts.note: an adder is a viper
to pan a camera is to sweep it across a scene

explanation.surface: A creature from Asia sweeping aside a snake as it strikes again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback of' gives the reversal, making REDDA, and 'blocking' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The red panda is a reddish mammal native to the Himalayas and China.

clue.text: 60s mum keeps home

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: mum, as in keeping mum, means silent
in means at home

explanation.surface: A mother in the 1960s staying at home.
explanation.walkthrough: '60s' looks like the decade but means sixty seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixty seconds make a single minute of time.

clue.text: Prime Minister's said there's no obvious exit from this

definitions.text: there's no obvious exit from this

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister, so the word means belonging to May

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister declares a situation has no easy way out.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was UK Prime Minister 2016-19; 'said' turns MAY'S into its soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A labyrinth of paths is designed so the way out is hard to find.

clue.text: Lament nun's straying and dissolution

indicators.note: straying means wandering off, so the letters of lament nun are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mourning a nun who has strayed from her order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straying' rearranges LAMENT NUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Annulment is the cancelling of a marriage or contract, the formal dissolution of it.

clue.text: Learner involved in giving treatment

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so the learner goes within the other word

parts.note: handing means passing or giving
L is a learner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A learner taking part in giving therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' puts L inside HANDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Handling is the way something or someone is dealt with, i.e. treatment.

clue.text: Cuckoo covetingly wanting condor's top endurance

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A crazed bird eyeing up a condor with envy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting condor's top' removes C from COVETINGLY; 'Cuckoo' rearranges OVETINGLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Longevity means long life or lasting a long time, close to endurance.

clue.text: Smart Aleck's main column's beginning in Telegraph

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word for telegraph

parts.note: a wire is a telegram, sent by telegraph
the main is the sea in old poetic usage

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A know-all writing the leading column in the Telegraph newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telegraph' looks like the newspaper but is WIRE; 'beginning' gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a person who pretends to be clever, a know-all.

clue.text: Surmise about South American city being poor

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the city

parts.note: to infer is to surmise or deduce
Rio de Janeiro in Brazil

explanation.surface: Speculating about a South American city's poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a reversal sign but here signals one word wrapping round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior means of low quality, so poor work is substandard work.

clue.text: Miss, born first of December

parts.note: née marks a woman's birth name, meaning born

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A young woman born at the start of December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a title but is a verb: to miss someone is to need them.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something can mean to lack it and want it.

clue.text: Hardship you reported squeezed into formal wear

indicators.note: squeezed into means forced inside, so the letter sits within the other word

parts.note: dress, as in evening dress, means formal clothing

indicators.note: reported means said, so the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Struggling to fit into a dinner suit, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' gives U from YOU; 'squeezed into' puts it inside DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress means constraint or compulsion; it is used loosely for hardship.

clue.text: With wings withdrawn, falcon over compartment

indicators.note: wings are the outer letters, so withdrawing them leaves the inner parts of both words

explanation.surface: A falcon folding its wings as it flies over an enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With wings withdrawn' takes the outer letters off FALCON and OVER, leaving ALCO and VE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess in a wall, a small compartment of a room.

clue.text: Timber article put in fine space

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the article goes within the other word

parts.note: OK means fine or acceptable
a is the indefinite article
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A wooden item placed in a nice open area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timber' is used as an adjective, as in 'timber frame'. An en is a printing space half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaken means made of oak, a hardwood, so wooden.

clue.text: Not all who use site take care of property

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not everyone who visits a website looks after property.
explanation.definitionFit: To house-sit is to live in someone's home and look after it while they are away.

clue.text: English player's sporting equipment

definitions.meaning: Jeremy ... is an English actor, a player on stage and screen

explanation.surface: The kit belonging to an English sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests a sportsman, but here it is an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers carry metal-headed clubs, and Jeremy is a well-known English actor bearing that surname.

clue.text: Heckle, dismissing one European king as fool

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to jeer is to heckle
E is the abbreviation for European
K is king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: Barracking a European monarch, dismissing him as an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing one European' drops one E from JEER, leaving JER.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerk is a slang insult for a stupid or contemptible person.

clue.text: Rival clubs locking small Parisian in changing room

indicators.note: locking means enclosing, so the small Parisian goes inside

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters of room are rearranged

parts.note: petit is French, the language of Paris, for small

explanation.surface: An opposing team shutting a little Frenchman in the dressing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges ROOM into OMOR; 'changing room' looks like a dressing room.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor is someone you contend against, a rival.

clue.text: Knight crazy about English rose regularly ignored beauties

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nuts means crazy
N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A knight mad about an English rose, ignoring the other beauties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses NUTS into STUN; 'regularly ignored' keeps R and S from ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunners are strikingly attractive people, so beauties.

clue.text: Harry Styles, most roguish

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The pop star Harry Styles described as the most mischievous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the singer's first name but is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly means cunning or mischievous, so its superlative is the most roguish.
